title: CHILDHOOD
text: the bitterness, the misery, the wretchedness of childhood

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Put me out of love with God.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I can't believe in God's goodness;

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I can believe

title: CHILDHOOD
text: In many avenging gods.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Most of all I believe

title: CHILDHOOD
text: In gods of bitter dullness,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Cruel local gods

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Who seared my childhood.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I've seen people put

title: CHILDHOOD
text: A chrysalis in a match-box,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: 'To see,' they told me, 'what sort of moth would come.'

title: CHILDHOOD
text: But when it broke its shell

title: CHILDHOOD
text: It slipped and stumbled and fell about its prison

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And tried to climb to the light

title: CHILDHOOD
text: For space to dry its wings.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: That's how I was.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Somebody found my chrysalis

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And shut it in a match-box.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: My shrivelled wings were beaten,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Shed their colours in dusty scales

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Before the box was opened

title: CHILDHOOD
text: For the moth to fly.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And then it was too late,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Because the beauty a child has,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And the beautiful things it learns before its birth,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Were shed, like moth-scales, from me.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I hate that town;

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I hate the town I lived in when I was little;

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I hate to think of it.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: There were always clouds, smoke, rain

title: CHILDHOOD
text: In that dingy little valley.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: It rained; it always rained.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I think I never saw the sun until I was nine--

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And then it was too late;

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Everything's too late after the first seven years.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: That long street we lived in

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Was duller than a drain

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And nearly as dingy.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: There were the big College

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And the pseudo-Gothic town-hall.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: There were the sordid provincial shops--

title: CHILDHOOD
text: The grocer's, and the shops for women,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: The shop where I bought transfers,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And the piano and gramaphone shop

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Where I used to stand

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Staring at the huge shiny pianos and at the pictures

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Of a white dog looking into a gramaphone.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: How dull and greasy and grey and sordid it was!

title: CHILDHOOD
text: On wet days--it was always wet--

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I used to kneel on a chair

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And look at it from the window.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: The dirty yellow trams

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Dragged noisily along

title: CHILDHOOD
text: With a clatter of wheels and bells

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And a humming of wires overhead.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: They threw up the filthy rain-water from the hollow lines

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And then the water ran back

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Full of brownish foam bubbles.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: There was nothing else to see--

title: CHILDHOOD
text: It was all so dull--

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Except a few grey legs under shiny black umbrellas

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Running along the grey shiny pavements;

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Sometimes there was a waggon

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Whose horses made a strange loud hollow sound

title: CHILDHOOD
text: With their hoofs

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Through the silent rain.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And there was a grey museum

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Full of dead birds and dead insects and dead animals

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And a few relics of the Romans--dead also.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: There was the sea-front,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: A long asphalt walk with a bleak road beside it,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Three piers, a row of houses,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And a salt dirty smell from the little harbour.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I was like a moth---

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Like one of those grey Emperor moths

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Which flutter through the vines at Capri.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And that damned little town was my match-box,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Against whose sides I beat and beat

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Until my wings were torn and faded, and dingy

title: CHILDHOOD
text: As that damned little town.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: At school it was just dull as that dull High Street.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: They taught me pothooks--

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I wanted to be alone, although I was so little,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Alone, away from the rain, the dingyness, the dullness,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Away somewhere else--

title: CHILDHOOD
text: The town was dull;

title: CHILDHOOD
text: The front was dull;

title: CHILDHOOD
text: The High Street and the other street were dull--

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And there was a public park, I remember,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And that was damned dull too,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: With its beds of geraniums no one was allowed to pick,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And its clipped lawns you weren't allowed to walk on,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And the gold-fish pond you mustn't paddle in,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And the gate made out of a whale's jaw-bones,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And the swings, which were for 'Board-School children,'

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And its gravel paths.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And on Sundays they rang the bells,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: From Baptist and Evangelical and Catholic churches.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: They had the Salvation Army.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I was taken to a High Church;

title: CHILDHOOD
text: The parson's name was Mowbray,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: 'Which is a good name but he thinks too much of it--'

title: CHILDHOOD
text: That's what I heard people say.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I took a little black book

title: CHILDHOOD
text: To that cold, grey, damp, smelling church,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And I had to sit on a hard bench,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Wriggle off it to kneel down when they sang psalms,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And wriggle off it to kneel down when they prayed--

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And then there was nothing to do

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Except to play trains with the hymn-books.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: There was nothing to see,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Nothing to do,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Nothing to play with,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Except that in an empty room upstairs

title: CHILDHOOD
text: There was a large tin box

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Containing reproductions of the Magna Charta,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Of the Declaration of Independence

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And of a letter from Raleigh after the Armada.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: There were also several packets of stamps,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Yellow and blue Guatemala parrots,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Blue stags and red baboons and birds from Sarawak,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Indians and Men-of-war

title: CHILDHOOD
text: From the United States,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: And the green and red portraits

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Of King Francobollo

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Of Italy.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I don't believe in God.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: I do believe in avenging gods

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Who plague us for sins we never sinned

title: CHILDHOOD
text: But who avenge us.

title: CHILDHOOD
text: That's why I'll never have a child,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Never shut up a chrysalis in a match-box

title: CHILDHOOD
text: For the moth to spoil and crush its bright colours,

title: CHILDHOOD
text: Beating its wings against the dingy prison-wall.

title: THE POPLAR
text: Why do you always stand there shivering

title: THE POPLAR
text: Between the white stream and the road?

title: THE POPLAR
text: The people pass through the dust

title: THE POPLAR
text: On bicycles, in carts, in motor-cars;

title: THE POPLAR
text: The waggoners go by at dawn;

title: THE POPLAR
text: The lovers walk on the grass path at night.

title: THE POPLAR
text: Stir from your roots, walk, poplar!

title: THE POPLAR
text: You are more beautiful than they are.

title: THE POPLAR
text: I know that the white wind loves you,

title: THE POPLAR
text: Is always kissing you and turning up

title: THE POPLAR
text: The white lining of your green petticoat.

title: THE POPLAR
text: The sky darts through you like blue rain,

title: THE POPLAR
text: And the grey rain drips on your flanks

title: THE POPLAR
text: And loves you.

title: THE POPLAR
text: And I have seen the moon

title: THE POPLAR
text: Slip his silver penny into your pocket

title: THE POPLAR
text: As you straightened your hair;

title: THE POPLAR
text: And the white mist curling and hesitating

title: THE POPLAR
text: Like a bashful lover about your knees.

title: THE POPLAR
text: I know you, poplar;

title: THE POPLAR
text: I have watched you since I was ten.

title: THE POPLAR
text: But if you had a little real love,

title: THE POPLAR
text: A little strength,

title: THE POPLAR
text: You would leave your nonchalant idle lovers

title: THE POPLAR
text: And go walking down the white road

title: THE POPLAR
text: Behind the waggoners.

title: THE POPLAR
text: There are beautiful beeches down beyond the hill.

title: THE POPLAR
text: Will you always stand there shivering?

title: ROUND-POND
text: Which puffs and spurts it into tiny pashing breakers

title: ROUND-POND
text: Dashed with lemon-yellow afternoon sunlight.

title: ROUND-POND
text: The shining of the sun upon the water

title: ROUND-POND
text: Is like a scattering of gold crocus-petals

title: ROUND-POND
text: In a long wavering irregular flight.

title: ROUND-POND
text: The water is cold to the eye

title: ROUND-POND
text: As the wind to the cheek.

title: ROUND-POND
text: In the budding chestnuts

title: ROUND-POND
text: Whose sticky buds glimmer and are half-burst open

title: ROUND-POND
text: The starlings make their clitter-clatter;

title: ROUND-POND
text: And the blackbirds in the grass

title: ROUND-POND
text: Are getting as fat as the pigeons.

title: ROUND-POND
text: Too-hoo, this is brave;

title: ROUND-POND
text: Even the cold wind is seeking a new mistress.

title: CATULLUS.
text: You were my playmate by the sea.

title: CATULLUS.
text: We swam together.

title: CATULLUS.
text: Your girl's body had no breasts.

title: CATULLUS.
text: We found prawns among the rocks;

title: CATULLUS.
text: We liked to feel the sun and to do nothing;

title: CATULLUS.
text: In the evening we played games with the others.

title: CATULLUS.
text: It made me glad to be by you.

title: CATULLUS.
text: Sometimes I kissed you,

title: CATULLUS.
text: And you were always glad to kiss me;

title: CATULLUS.
text: But I was afraid--I was only fourteen.

title: CATULLUS.
text: And I had quite forgotten you,

title: CATULLUS.
text: You and your name.

title: CATULLUS.
text: To-day I pass through the streets.

title: CATULLUS.
text: She who touches my arm and talks with me

title: CATULLUS.
text: Is--who knows?--Helen of Sparta,

title: CATULLUS.
text: Dryope, Laodamia....

title: CATULLUS.
text: And there are you

title: CATULLUS.

title: A GIRL

title: A GIRL
text: That pains our thought even now.

text: You were the notes

text: Of cold fantastic grief

title: A GIRL

text: After her dead flowers,

text: You are clear,

title: THE GARDEN
text: O rose, cut in rock,

text: I could scrape the colour

title: THE GARDEN
text: from the petal,

text: If I could break you

text: If I could stir

text: O wind,

text: Fruit can not drop

title: THE GARDEN
text: through this thick air:

title: THE GARDEN
text: the points of pears

title: SEA LILY
text: Reed,

title: SEA LILY
text: slashed and torn,

title: SEA LILY
text: but doubly rich--

title: SEA LILY
text: such great heads as yours

title: SEA LILY
text: drift upon temple-steps,

title: SEA LILY
text: but you are shattered

title: SEA LILY
text: in the wind.

title: SEA LILY
text: Myrtle-bark

title: SEA LILY
text: is flecked from you,

title: SEA LILY
text: scales are dashed

title: SEA LILY
text: from your stem,

title: SEA LILY
text: sand cuts your petal,

title: SEA LILY
text: furrows it with hard edge,

title: SEA LILY
text: like flint

title: SEA LILY
text: on a bright stone.

title: SEA LILY
text: Yet though the whole wind

title: SEA LILY

title: SEA LILY
text: you are lifted up,

title: SEA LILY
text: aye--though it hiss

text: Weed, moss-weed,

title: SEA IRIS
text: root tangled in sand,

title: SEA IRIS
text: sea-iris, brittle flower,

title: SEA IRIS
text: one petal like a shell

title: SEA IRIS
text: is broken,

title: SEA IRIS
text: and you print a shadow

title: SEA IRIS
text: like a thin twig.

title: SEA IRIS
text: Fortunate one,

title: SEA IRIS
text: scented and stinging,

title: SEA IRIS
text: rigid myrrh-bud,

title: SEA IRIS
text: camphor-flower,

title: SEA IRIS
text: sweet and salt--you are wind

text: in our nostrils.
